title: Counterexamples or Direct Corrections for Novice Programmers?
grain: Either an author-published learner/problem summary or an independently published anonymized source-code attempt
dataset: CSEDM 2019 published ITAP cross-validation rows and the Refactory novice programming corpus
question: Should a beginner receive an elicited counterexample or a direct correction after a repeatable misconception?
design: Use the 2019 challenge authors' public predictions and real first-correct, any-hint and attempt records. Hold out entire learners and mature earlier learners before fitting. Independently inspect real duplicate-removal attempts in the Refactory corpus. Build two runnable feedback designs and specify equal exposure, a new transfer item and a prospective learner-randomized evaluation.
boundary: The public CSEDM example describes a subset of the 89-learner, 38-task source cohort. It contains aggregated learner/problem outcomes. Actual code examples are from the independent Refactory study. No newly delivered hint or transfer improvement is attributed to either cohort.
redistribution: Only derived features and public author example labels are included; no raw student programs are redistributed. Source teams and distribution terms are identified.

fields.prior_rate: Previously correct fraction supplied by CSEDM
fields.prior_attempts: Earlier attempts summary supplied by authors
fields.mutates: Static iteration/removal pattern; empty if Python syntax could not be parsed
